title: Impact of Unexpected Dovish Fed Announcements on Bank Stock Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Event Study methodology is appropriate here. We examine abnormal returns around the Fed announcement (event_day = 0) by comparing actual returns to expected returns based on a market model. The key assumption is that in the absence of the Fed announcement, stock returns would follow their normal relationship with market returns as estimated from the pre-event period. We'll use days -10 to -2 as the estimation window and days -1 to +5 as the event window.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s60_data.csv")

# Define windows
estimation_window <- c(-10, -2)
event_window <- c(-1, 5)

# Function to calculate abnormal returns for each stock
calculate_abnormal_returns <- function(stock_data) {
  # Estimation period data
  est_data <- stock_data[stock_data$event_day >= estimation_window[1] & 
                        stock_data$event_day <= estimation_window[2], ]
  
  # Market model: ret = alpha + beta * mkt_ret + error
  model <- lm(ret ~ mkt_ret, data = est_data)
  alpha <- coef(model)[1]
  beta_est <- coef(model)[2]
  
  # Calculate abnormal returns for event window
  event_data <- stock_data[stock_data$event_day >= event_window[1] & 
                          stock_data$event_day <= event_window[2], ]
  
  event_data$expected_ret <- alpha + beta_est * event_data$mkt_ret
  event_data$abnormal_ret <- event_data$ret - event_data$expected_ret
  
  return(event_data)
}

# Calculate abnormal returns for each stock
results_list <- list()
for(stock in unique(data$stock_id)) {
  stock_data <- data[data$stock_id == stock, ]
  results_list[[as.character(stock)]] <- calculate_abnormal_returns(stock_data)
}

# Combine results
abnormal_returns <- do.call(rbind, results_list)

# Calculate average abnormal returns (AAR) for each event day
aar <- abnormal_returns %>%
  group_by(event_day) %>%
  summarise(
    AAR = mean(abnormal_ret, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_stocks = n(),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

print("Average Abnormal Returns (AAR) by Event Day:")
print(aar)

# Calculate Cumulative Average Abnormal Returns (CAAR)
aar$CAAR <- cumsum(aar$AAR)

print("\nCumulative Average Abnormal Returns (CAAR):")
print(aar[, c("event_day", "CAAR")])

# Statistical significance test for CAAR
# Calculate standard error of abnormal returns
abnormal_returns_summary <- abnormal_returns %>%
  group_by(event_day) %>%
  summarise(
    AAR = mean(abnormal_ret, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE_AAR = sd(abnormal_ret, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    n_stocks = n(),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# Add t-statistics and p-values
abnormal_returns_summary$t_stat <- abnormal_returns_summary$AAR / abnormal_returns_summary$SE_AAR
abnormal_returns_summary$p_value <- 2 * pt(-abs(abnormal_returns_summary$t_stat), 
                                          df = abnormal_returns_summary$n_stocks - 1)

print("\nStatistical Significance of AAR:")
print(abnormal_returns_summary[, c("event_day", "AAR", "t_stat", "p_value")])

# Key results
event_day_0_car <- aar[aar$event_day == 0, "CAAR"]
total_car <- tail(aar$CAAR, 1)

cat("\n=== KEY RESULTS ===\n")
cat("Cumulative Abnormal Return on Event Day (0):", round(event_day_0_car * 100, 3), "%\n")
cat("Total CAR over event window (-1 to +5):", round(total_car * 100, 3), "%\n")

# Robustness check 1: Alternative event window (-2 to +2)
alt_event_data <- abnormal_returns[abnormal_returns$event_day >= -2 & 
                                  abnormal_returns$event_day <= 2, ]
alt_car <- sum(alt_event_data %>% group_by(event_day) %>% 
               summarise(AAR = mean(abnormal_ret, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop') %>% 
               pull(AAR))

cat("Robustness Check - CAR (-2 to +2):", round(alt_car * 100, 3), "%\n")

# Robustness check 2: Cross-sectional test
# Test if CAR is significantly different from zero across stocks
stock_cars <- abnormal_returns %>%
  filter(event_day >= -1 & event_day <= 5) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(stock_car = sum(abnormal_ret, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')

car_t_test <- t.test(stock_cars$stock_car, mu = 0)
cat("Cross-sectional t-test for CAR significance: t =", round(car_t_test$statistic, 3), 
    ", p-value =", round(car_t_test$p.value, 4), "\n")

# Plot results
plot_data <- aar
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = event_day, y = CAAR * 100)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue", size = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "red", size = 2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
  labs(title = "Cumulative Average Abnormal Returns Around Fed Announcement",
       x = "Event Day", y = "CAAR (%)") +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave("car_plot.png", width = 10, height = 6)
cat("Plot saved as car_plot.png\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect to find positive cumulative abnormal returns for bank stocks following unexpected dovish Fed announcements, with a magnitude of approximately 2-4% over the event window. This is because dovish monetary policy typically involves lower interest rates or easier credit conditions, which benefit banks through: (1) improved loan demand, (2) reduced funding costs, (3) lower probability of loan defaults, and (4) overall positive sentiment toward financial sector stocks. The effect should be most pronounced on the announcement day (event_day = 0) and the following day, with some anticipation effects possibly visible on day -1.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare bank stock returns around the event day to assess the impact of the announcement.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Unexpected dovish Fed announcements lead to a decrease in bank stock CAR.
